title: First-Principles Proof of the Work-Energy Theorem for Particle Motion
target_equation: W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K = \frac{1}{2} m v_f^2 - \frac{1}{2} m v_i^2
assumptions: Newton's Second Law F_net = m dv/dt
starting_principles: Definition of net work as path line integral W_net = int F_net . dr

ordered_steps.explanation: Substitute Newton's Second Law F_net = m dv/dt into the work line integral.
Express velocity vector v = dr/dt and utilize differential scalar product d(v . v) = 2 v . dv.
Recognize that v . dv = v dv, converting vector line integral into standard 1D scalar integral over speed.
ordered_steps.equation_latex: W_{\text{net}} = m \int_{v_i}^{v_f} v \, dv = m \left[ \frac{v^2}{2} \right]_{v_i}^{v_f} = \frac{1}{2} m v_f^2 - \frac{1}{2} m v_i^2 = \Delta K

limiting_cases: When net work is zero, Delta K = 0 implying speed magnitude remains invariant (e.g. uniform circular motion)
When initial speed v_i = 0, W_net = 1/2 m v_f^2, representing work done to accelerate body from rest
claim_traces: HCV1 Ch 8 p. 132; HRW Ch 7 p. 174; UP Ch 6 p. 208
